payload.title: Connectivity vs. spatial arrangement

visualCard.title: Isomer Classification & Index of Hydrogen Deficiency (IHD / Degrees of Unsaturation)
visualCard.formula: IHD = [2C + 2 + N − H − X] / 2   (O and divalent S have 0 effect on IHD)

items.label: 1 IHD Unit
items.text: Equals 1 ring OR 1 π bond (alkene C=C or carbonyl C=O).

items.label: 2 IHD Units
items.text: Equals 1 alkyne (C≡C), 2 double bonds, 2 rings, or 1 ring + 1 double bond (benzene = 4 IHD).

payload.title: Conformations and ring strain
payload.fullNote: Angle strain is deviation from preferred bond angles; torsional strain comes from eclipsing bonds; nonbonded (steric) strain comes from crowding of atoms not bonded to each other. Butane anti and gauche conformations are staggered, but gauche has greater methyl–methyl crowding. A cyclohexane chair has nearly ideal angles and staggered bonds; bulky substituents usually prefer equatorial sites to reduce 1,3-diaxial crowding.

visualCard.title: Newman Dihedral Energy & Cyclohexane Chair Ring-Flip Mechanics

items.label: Newman Staggered Conformers
items.text: Anti (180° between bulky groups) is lowest energy; Gauche (60°) has a small steric penalty (~3.8 kJ/mol for butane methyls).

items.label: Newman Eclipsed Transitions
items.text: Eclipsed (120°) has torsional strain; Syn-periplanar (0° bulky-bulky) is the highest-energy barrier (~19 kJ/mol in butane).

items.label: Cyclohexane Chair Ring Flip
items.text: Eliminates angle and torsional strain (0° eclipsing); ring flip converts ALL Axial ⇄ Equatorial while UP stays UP and DOWN stays DOWN.

visualCard.title: 1,4- vs 1,3- vs 1,2-Disubstituted Cyclohexane Cis/Trans Cheat Sheet
visualCard.prompt: What changes and what stays fixed during a cyclohexane chair flip?

items.label: Axial vs. Equatorial Status
items.text: Every axial bond becomes equatorial and every equatorial bond becomes axial to relieve 1,3-diaxial steric clashes.

items.label: Up / Down Wedge-Dash Face
items.text: A ring flip is a conformational rotation, not bond breaking: cis remains cis and R/S stereocenters never invert.

items.label: tert-Butyl Conformational Lock
items.text: A bulky tert-butyl group experiences massive 1,3-diaxial strain if axial, locking the chair so t-Bu stays equatorial.

visualCard.title: Equating "Cis" with "Both Equatorial" or Thinking Ring Flips Invert R/S

items.label: Common Trap
items.text: Assuming cis-1,2-dimethylcyclohexane is diequatorial or that a chair flip turns cis into trans.

items.label: Correct Reasoning
items.text: Alternate Up/Down around the ring: 1,2-cis is (ax,eq), 1,3-cis is (eq,eq) or (ax,ax), and 1,4-trans is (eq,eq) or (ax,ax).

items.label: β-D-Glucopyranose

visualCard.title: Assuming Every Molecule with Stereocenters Is Chiral (The Meso Trap)

items.label: Common Trap
items.text: Counting n = 2 stereocenters in 2,3-dibromobutane and immediately answering "4 optically active stereoisomers".

items.label: Correct Reasoning
items.text: Always check for a plane of symmetry: symmetric 2,3-disubstituted chains have ONLY 3 stereoisomers (1 enantiomeric pair + 1 achiral meso).

payload.title: Chirality, enantiomers, and meso compounds
payload.fullNote: Enantiomers have the same ordinary properties in achiral environments but opposite optical rotations under matched conditions; chiral receptors can distinguish them. A suitable single-enantiomer resolving agent can convert a racemate into diastereomeric salts or derivatives. Their different properties permit separation, followed by regeneration of the original enantiomers. Chiral chromatography is another approach.

visualCard.title: Chiral Drug Receptor Binding (Thalidomide, Albuterol) & Enzyme Specificity

items.label: Chiral Receptor Pocket

payload.title: CIP priorities and Fischer projections
payload.fullNote:
Rank directly attached atoms by atomic number; isotopes by mass. Resolve ties one sphere at a time using sorted atom lists. Treat multiple bonds with duplicate-atom bookkeeping. With priority 4 away, clockwise 1→2→3 is R and counterclockwise is S.

Absolute configuration assigns a stereochemical arrangement independently (for example R/S). Relative configuration describes a relationship to another stereocenter or reference compound. A remote chemical change can retain the local spatial arrangement while changing CIP priorities and therefore its R/S label; reassess priorities instead of equating a letter change with physical inversion.

visualCard.title: Cahn-Ingold-Prelog (CIP) Absolute Configuration (R / S) & Fischer Projections

items.label: Rank 4 Groups by Atomic Number (Z)
items.text: Compare directly attached atoms first (I > Br > Cl > S > P > F > O > N > C > H); heavier isotopes win ties (³H > ²H > ¹H).

items.label: Move Outward to First Point of Difference
items.text: List attached atoms in decreasing Z order—the single highest atomic number wins (e.g., –CH₂Br beats –C(CH₃)₃ because Br > C).

items.label: Orient Priority #4 & Trace 1 → 2 → 3
items.text: With group #4 on a DASH: Clockwise = R (Rectus), Counterclockwise = S (Sinister). If #4 is on a WEDGE, reverse the result.

items.text: Never add atomic numbers! Compare the single highest-Z atom at the tiebreaker shell: O (Z=8) beats C (Z=6), so –CH₂OH wins.

lesson.title: Optical activity, specific rotation, and resolution

steps.label: 1. Geometry is not optical sign
steps.text: Butan-2-ol can exist as enantiomers. Its connectivity alone does not specify which enantiomer is present, and an R/S descriptor does not predict (+)/(−). Measure the rotation experimentally.

steps.label: 2. Normalize a measurement
steps.text: Illustrative data: αobs = +1.2°, c = 0.040 g/mL and l = 10 cm = 1.0 dm. Then [α] = +1.2/(0.040 × 1.0) = +30 °·mL·g⁻¹·dm⁻¹. These are practice numbers, not a tabulated value for the displayed connectivity.

steps.label: 3. Resolve a racemate
steps.text: For a suitable substrate, use a single-enantiomer resolving agent to make diastereomeric salts or derivatives. Separate them by a suitable property difference, then regenerate the starting enantiomers. Ordinary achiral distillation does not generally separate enantiomers, which share the same boiling point under achiral conditions.

payload.title: Optical activity, specific rotation, and resolution
payload.fullNote: Observed optical rotation αobs depends on concentration, path length, wavelength, temperature and solvent. In the common solution convention, [α] = αobs/(l × c), with l in dm and c in g/mL. If αobs is in degrees, the corresponding specific-rotation units are °·mL·g⁻¹·dm⁻¹. State wavelength, temperature and solvent when comparing measurements.

lessonInventory.title: Connectivity vs. spatial arrangement
lessonInventory.tag: Same formula is only the first test
lessonInventory.coreRule: Constitutional isomers share a molecular formula but differ in connectivity. Stereoisomers have the same connectivity and differ in spatial arrangement. Conformers interconvert by rotations about single bonds.

lessonInventory.title: Conformations and ring strain
lessonInventory.coreRule: Angle strain is deviation from preferred bond angles; torsional strain comes from eclipsing bonds; nonbonded (steric) strain comes from crowding of atoms not bonded to each other. Butane anti and gauche conformations are staggered, but gauche has greater methyl–methyl crowding. A cyclohexane chair has nearly ideal angles and staggered bonds; bulky substituents usually prefer equatorial sites to reduce 1,3-diaxial crowding.

lessonInventory.title: Chirality, enantiomers, and meso compounds
lessonInventory.tag: Mirror image ≠ always a different molecule
lessonInventory.coreRule: A tetrahedral carbon with four different substituents is a common stereogenic center. Enantiomers are nonsuperimposable mirror images. Diastereomers are stereoisomers that are not mirror images; E/Z pairs qualify too.

lessonInventory.title: CIP priorities and Fischer projections
lessonInventory.coreRule:
Rank directly attached atoms by atomic number; isotopes by mass. Resolve ties one sphere at a time using sorted atom lists. Treat multiple bonds with duplicate-atom bookkeeping. With priority 4 away, clockwise 1→2→3 is R and counterclockwise is S.
Absolute configuration assigns a stereochemical arrangement independently (for example R/S). Relative configuration describes a relationship to another stereocenter or reference compound. A remote chemical change can retain the local spatial arrangement while changing CIP priorities and therefore its R/S label; reassess priorities instead of equating a letter change with physical inversion.

lessonInventory.title: E/Z configuration and achirality
lessonInventory.coreRule: E/Z is defined only if each double-bond carbon has two different substituents. Rank each end by CIP: Z puts the higher-priority groups on the same side; E puts them on opposite sides. E/Z geometry alone does not determine whether a whole molecule is chiral.

lessonInventory.title: Optical activity, specific rotation, and resolution
lessonInventory.tag: Measure rotation; normalize units; keep configuration labels separate
lessonInventory.coreRule: Observed optical rotation αobs depends on concentration, path length, wavelength, temperature and solvent. In the common solution convention, [α] = αobs/(l × c), with l in dm and c in g/mL. If αobs is in degrees, the corresponding specific-rotation units are °·mL·g⁻¹·dm⁻¹. State wavelength, temperature and solvent when comparing measurements.
